metadata.title: AyurBot demonstration knowledge base
metadata.description: Editable educational knowledge base for AyurBot. All entries are demonstration data summarising traditional Ayurvedic descriptions.
metadata.disclaimer: Traditional Ayurvedic descriptions are not clinical evidence. This data has not been clinically validated and must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dosing.

source.description: Compiled for this educational prototype from widely repeated summaries of classical Ayurvedic descriptions. Not checked line-by-line against a specific monograph or edition.
source.suggested_verification: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India (Government of India, Ministry of AYUSH) and the classical texts it cites.

entries.evidence_note: Traditional Ayurvedic description. This is not evidence of clinical efficacy or safety for any modern medical condition.
entries.summary: Tulsi is an aromatic plant that classical Ayurvedic descriptions associate mainly with the respiratory system and with Kapha and Vata.

traditional_uses.description: Described in Ayurvedic literature in the context of Kasa (cough as a classical symptom category).
Described in the context of Shwasa (classical category of breathing difficulty).
Described in the context of Pratishyaya (classical category resembling nasal catarrh).
Described in the context of Jwara (classical fever category).

dosha_associations.note: Dosha effects are traditional classifications, not measured physiological effects.

safety_notes: Concentrated extracts are different from culinary or household use; their safety profile is not established by this knowledge base.
People who are pregnant, breastfeeding, taking regular medication or preparing for surgery should consult a qualified healthcare professional before using any herbal product.

entries.summary: Haridra (turmeric rhizome) is described in classical Ayurveda mainly in relation to the skin, wounds and Kapha.

traditional_uses.description: Described in the context of Kushtha (a broad classical group of skin conditions).
Described in the context of Kandu (itching).
Described in the context of Vrana (wounds and ulcers), often as external application.
Described in the context of Prameha (a classical group of urinary and metabolic conditions).

dosha_associations.note: Classical sources differ on its effect on Vata and Pitta, so only Kapha is listed here.

safety_notes: Culinary turmeric and concentrated curcumin supplements are not equivalent.

Case reports have linked some turmeric or curcumin supplements to liver injury; anyone with liver disease, gallbladder problems or who takes blood-thinning or other regular medication should ask a qualified professional first.

entries.summary: Ashwagandha root is classed in Ayurveda as a Rasayana (rejuvenative) and Balya (strength-promoting) herb, chiefly associated with Vata.

traditional_uses.description: Described in the context of Daurbalya (general weakness or debility).
Described in the context of Vata Vyadhi (a classical group of disorders attributed to Vata).
Described in the context of Anidra (classical term for sleeplessness).

dosha_associations.note: Because of its Ushna (heating) virya, some descriptions caution about excess Pitta.

safety_notes: Ashwagandha products have been associated with rare reports of liver injury.
Commonly advised against during pregnancy; people with thyroid conditions, autoimmune conditions or who take sedatives or other regular medication should consult a qualified professional.

entries.summary: Brahmi is described in Ayurveda as a Medhya (intellect-supporting) Rasayana.

traditional_uses.description: Described in the context of weak memory (Smriti) and learning.
Described in the context of Unmada (classical category of mental disturbance).
Described in the context of Apasmara (classical category of seizure-like episodes).

dosha_associations.note: Some sources describe Brahmi as balancing all three doshas.

entries.ambiguity_note: In parts of India the name Brahmi is also used for Centella asiatica (Mandukaparni). This entry refers to Bacopa monnieri.
safety_notes: Digestive upset has been reported with Bacopa products.
Anyone taking medication for thyroid conditions, seizures or mood, or who is pregnant, should consult a qualified professional.

entries.summary: Guduchi stem is described in classical Ayurveda as a Rasayana that is traditionally said to balance all three doshas.

traditional_uses.description: Described in the context of Jwara (classical fever category), including recurring fevers.
Described in the context of Prameha.
Described in the context of Kamala (classical term involving yellow discoloration).
Described in the context of Vatarakta (classical joint and blood-related disorder).

dosha_associations.note: Traditionally described as Tridoshashamaka (balancing all three doshas).

safety_notes: Published case series have described liver injury in some people using Guduchi (Giloy) products; causality and product identity have been debated.
Anyone with liver disease, autoimmune disease or diabetes medication, or who is pregnant, should consult a qualified professional.

entries.summary: Neem (Nimba) is a strongly bitter tree described in Ayurveda mainly for the skin and for Kapha and Pitta.

traditional_uses.description: Described in the context of Kushtha (classical skin-condition group).
Described in the context of Kandu (itching).
Described in the context of Krimi (classical category of worms and parasites).
Described in the context of Vrana (wounds), often as external application.

dosha_associations.note: Its bitter, dry qualities are traditionally said to increase Vata.

safety_notes: Swallowing neem oil has caused serious poisoning in young children; neem oil must be kept away from children.
Not advised during pregnancy or when trying to conceive without professional guidance.

entries.summary: Vata is the dosha of movement in Ayurvedic theory, made up of the space and air elements.
functions: Breathing and circulation (as described in Ayurvedic theory)
entries.evidence_note: Doshas are explanatory concepts of Ayurvedic theory, not measurable biomedical entities.

entries.summary: Virya is the potency of a substance, usually classed as Ushna (hot) or Sheeta (cold).
